Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "the dye log for the west room has an entry for the indigo batch from tuesday, and the cost is being read as $130.73 in the copy that was passed around. that is not the right amount. the paper log has $50.46 for the indigo used on the cotton test pieces, and that is the actual cost, not $130.73. the higher amount appears in the margin beside the entry, but there is no note there explaining it, so it should not be treated as the batch cost. the log also lists the dye lot as ID-24B and says that two test pieces were recorded. i checked the amounts against the written entry, and the $50.46 figure is clear. please make sure the record says the correct amount and does not leave the other figure looking like an alternate cost. the rest of the entry can stay as it is, including the dye lot and the note about the two pieces.", "output": "The dye log for the west room has an entry for Tuesday’s indigo batch, and a circulated copy shows the cost as $130.73. That is not the correct amount. The paper log records $50.46 for the indigo used on the cotton test pieces; the actual cost was $50.46, not $130.73. The log also lists the dye lot as ID-24B and records two test pieces. I checked the amounts against the written entry, and the $50.46 figure is clear. Please make sure the record shows the correct amount and does not leave the other figure looking like an alternate cost. The rest of the entry can stay as it is, including the dye lot and the note about the two pieces."}]
